sources.author: Teodoro Díaz Zavala
sources.edition: Publisher chapter extract; exact publication year not independently established from the acquired extract.
sources.actual_material_read: Chapter title and author page (PDF1/printed198); regional mountain passage prose (PDF14/printed211); hydrography prose (PDF23–26/printed220–223); water-resources prose (PDF40/printed237); Pedregal-basin conservation prose (PDF46/printed243); relevant bibliography (PDF86–87/printed283–284). Original pixels inspected for title page, Figure19 climate map and surrounding text (PDF24/printed221), and Mitare hydrography paragraph (PDF26/printed223). Other original map pixels are not claimed as inspected.
sources.independence_basis: The actual chapter title and author identify the Fundación Empresas Polar regional geography project. It is distinct in publishing project and content from the stopped Hackley national geology map, DCN La Victoria sheet, Guanipa biological-paper clue and regional OAS projects. Figure19 credits Rigoberto Andressen’s GeoVenezuela climate-map work; it is used only as broad thematic geography, never as river-course proof.
sources.limits: The independently authored chapter provides bounded regional prose but no inspected corridor-scale river map. Separate cartographic-appendix sheets referred to in the text were not acquired or inspected. The extract does not establish present flow, active reservoir operation, precise name boundaries or formal registry status.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen western headward approach and Caviar Creek
correspondence.finding: The chosen opening lies along the western headward approach to the mapped Caviar Creek valley. The original depicts the short western feeder joining the named Caviar Creek channel and its continuous northward course. The selected line is locally displaced onto the valley side and straightens bends; correspondence is at ordinary valley scale. Caviar Creek is labelled on the receiving tributary, while the short initial western feeder has no name established here. The chosen point is not asserted to be the ultimate natural source.

correspondence.component_scope: Caviar Creek transition into the upper Koyuk corridor
correspondence.finding: The map follows Caviar Creek north and then east into the connected river corridor repeatedly labelled Koyuk River. The western and northern tributary approaches and the intervening confluence setting are visible. The selected northern corner and eastward straight segments generalize the mapped bends and their broad valley; the Caviar name is retained for its distinct tributary reach rather than replaced with Koyuk throughout.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper Koyuk River and Knowles Creek junction
correspondence.finding: Repeated Koyuk River labels follow the continuous eastward channel through the upper valley, its locally divided channel section and the Knowles Creek junction. Overlapping maps carry the route into the more open, pond-rich floodplain. Adjacent ponds and lateral tributaries do not require a separate lake-to-lake transfer along the selected river corridor.

correspondence.component_scope: Middle Koyuk River and Big Bar Creek to First Chance Creek
correspondence.finding: The connected Koyuk channel continues east through large bends, receives Big Bar Creek and reaches the First Chance Creek junction before turning south. All selected intermediate parts are covered by the readable original. The surrounding lakes, oxbows and tributary channels remain distinct from the named through-river.

correspondence.component_scope: Southward middle reach and the Copper and June Creek joins
correspondence.finding: The original depicts Koyuk River continuously through the long southward meander belt, past the Copper Creek and June Creek joins, and around its eastward turn. Selected straight segments cut bends and some floodplain ponds but correspond to the same connected receiving-river corridor at ordinary scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Koyuk floodplain and Peace River junction
correspondence.finding: The river continues east and southeast through a wide meander and oxbow belt. The original directly shows the Peace River confluence and the Willow Creek and Stephensons Stream approaches, followed by the downstream Koyuk bends. Repeated labels and continuous mapped channels establish the through-corridor; lateral lakes are not assigned the river name.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower bend, tributary joins and southward delta approach
correspondence.finding: The map follows the lower Koyuk past the Kenwood Creek setting, the northeastern tributary junction and the broad bend into the southward channel. Alameda Creek and smaller feeders join the lower course. The main river remains continuously depicted to the delta approach; no reservoir, glacier or managed-water transfer occurs in this selected portion.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual selected endpoint in the Koyuk delta complex
correspondence.finding: The selected lower route enters the mapped Koyuk River delta, where broad channels divide around islands and wetland areas. Its actual endpoint lies inside this delta complex, on the inner side of the lower bend upstream of the coastal outlet near Koyuk. The last straight segment cuts the river bend and island-rich delta setting; it is a generalized terminal representation, not a demonstrated separate cross-island waterway. Ordinary delta-system correspondence is established. The selected endpoint is not called the exact marine mouth, and no particular current distributary or shoreline position is assigned.

correspondence.component_scope: opening
correspondence.finding: The chosen southwestern opening crosses the western margin of the Torreón sheet. The acquired full-sheet overview was inspected only at regional scale; no sufficiently readable, selected-route comparison of the opening or its join was completed. No headwater name is assigned.

correspondence.component_scope: western_approach
correspondence.finding: The selected western arc requires the adjacent Santiago Papasquiaro cartographic footprint and the join back into Torreón. Its original was obtained before the later stop but never visually or textually read. Geographic and natural-channel continuity are unestablished.

correspondence.component_scope: central_turn_and_plain
correspondence.finding: The Torreón overview shows regional relief, populated agricultural plain and a hydrographic/infrastructure network. At the inspected overview scale, the actual selected turn, intermediate joins and eastward path could not be reliably distinguished from neighboring natural channels or managed connections. Neither a named continuous river nor a canal transfer is established.

correspondence.component_scope: northeastern_plain_and_sheet_join
correspondence.finding: The selection continues northeast from the central plain into the Tlahualilo sheet footprint. The required detailed source-to-route correspondence and selected cross-sheet through-link were not observed. Regional drainage membership is not evidence of that connection.

correspondence.component_scope: northern_curve_and_actual_terminal
correspondence.finding: The northern bend and actual terminal lack an inspected primary source. No lake entry, reservoir connection, canal transfer, disappearing-stream end, or named receiving channel is assigned.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen eastern opening and initial Kashunuk bend
correspondence.finding: The chosen eastern opening is in the mapped Kashunuk River corridor. The connected channel bends south and west before turning north around the elongated floodplain bend. Direct Kashunuk River labels identify this upper selected channel. The opening is a selected interior river position, not an assertion of the ultimate natural source. The generalized line cuts the large bend, but the original map visibly supplies the connected river corridor.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper Kashunuk return bend and southwestern continuation
correspondence.finding: The northern turn joins the southwestern continuation of the same repeatedly labelled Kashunuk River. The original shows connected main-channel bends, nearby side-channel junctions and numerous lateral lakes and abandoned-channel shapes. All selected intervals through the long southwestward turn and succeeding westward bend have continuous river-corridor correspondence. No transfer through a separate isolated lake is required; straight selected pieces locally shortcut the meanders.

correspondence.component_scope: Middle Kashunuk westward loops and branch joins
correspondence.finding: The named Kashunuk course runs through successive broad loops, bends west across a divided river reach and turns southwest. The map shows the bifurcating and rejoining channel arms around intervening islands and floodplain strips. These visible through-links cover every selected intermediate part and join. Adjacent lake-rich wetland is contextual rather than evidence for an invented cross-wetland connection.

correspondence.component_scope: Kashunuk southwestern turn and southeastward widening
correspondence.finding: The connected Kashunuk channel turns south and then southeast into a wider river corridor. Repeated main-channel labels distinguish it from the nearby Kokechik River to the west and other side streams. The mapped main channel and connected lateral arms establish the selected route and its intermediate joins across the full interval. The selection shifts across island and floodplain edges as it generalizes the mapped bends; this does not establish separate channels along those shortcuts.

correspondence.component_scope: Nanvaranak Choa widening and connected southern passage
correspondence.finding: The original depicts an openly connected widening labelled Nanvaranak Choa beside Kashunuk River labels, with a continuous southern passage returning to the broad Kashunuk corridor. The selected passage, including its turn at the south side of the widening, is covered. Nanvaranak Choa is retained as a distinct mapped waterbody label, not renamed as a river or assumed to be an isolated lake.

correspondence.component_scope: Expanded Kashunuk reach past Nushkolik Mountain
correspondence.finding: The river expands into a broad connected waterway east and south of Nushkolik Mountain and then turns west and southwest. The Nungatak River approach and other side-channel openings are visible. Repeated Kashunuk River labels continue across the widening and its narrower connecting reach. Every selected intervening part lies within this ordinary named corridor; no unviewed lake-to-river or wetland transfer remains.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Kashunuk branching and Aphrewn receiving continuation
correspondence.finding: The original shows the lower Kashunuk bends and a western branch that retains the Kashunuk River name. The selected route instead follows the broad connected southward continuation, which is repeatedly labelled Aphrewn River farther along. Both the channel split and the selected southward through-connection are visible. The two names remain bounded to their mapped reaches; no precise legal or cartographic name-change vertex is assigned.

correspondence.component_scope: Aphrewn River and actual selected terminal
correspondence.finding: The original repeatedly labels the broad southern channel Aphrewn River and depicts its connected meanders through the wetland-and-pond plain. All selected final parts and the actual stored endpoint correspond to that channel at ordinary corridor scale. The endpoint is inside a mapped Aphrewn bend, and the map visibly continues the river farther southwest. It is not identified as the natural ocean mouth. The selected path locally cuts large bends, but the original establishes the continuous receiving channel without any material missing through-link.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen southwestern opening and first eastward headward corridor
correspondence.finding: The complete chosen opening and eastern sequence were considered from the supplied selection. The chapter identifies the Mitare drainage and its named tributaries but supplies no usable channel map tying this particular opening or its first joins to a named branch. No Pedregal, Japure, Mamón, Paraíso or Juan Negro name is assigned to these selected parts.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper northeastward corridor and intervening bends
correspondence.finding: The selected upper route continues northeast and then north through several bends. Regional prose distinguishes the Pedregal tributary, its Japure and Mamón contributors, and the Paraíso tributary with Juan Negro. These are documented basin relationships, not identification of the particular selected channel or its intervening junctions.

correspondence.component_scope: Middle northeastward corridor and transition toward the northward valley
correspondence.finding: The chapter does not provide ordinary corridor-scale cartography or a route description detailed enough to establish this selected middle interval and its joins. The named tributary relationships cannot establish which tributary the selection follows.

correspondence.component_scope: Northward middle valley and tributary/reservoir relationship
correspondence.finding: The source records a Pedregal reservoir that became silted up, and later describes the protected Pedregal basin. No source material read establishes where this impoundment lies relative to the selected route, or verifies a selected inlet, crossing, outlet or managed through-link. The existence of a reservoir elsewhere in the named basin is not taken as evidence that the selected path crosses it.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower northward corridor toward the coastal plain
correspondence.finding: The chapter describes Mitare passing Sabaneta and then Mitare before reaching Golfete de Coro, and identifies a mountain passage as Mitare or Sabaneta. This supports a regional receiving-river candidate. Without a channel map, correspondence of the selected lower bends and local joins remains unestablished. The regional alias is not assigned to every upstream selected reach.

correspondence.component_scope: Final deltaic passage and actual coastal terminal
correspondence.finding: The actual selected endpoint and final deltaic approach were considered. Source prose puts the Mitare mouth in Golfete de Coro and describes its sedimentary coastal setting near Punta Caimán. The inspected climate map shows broad coast and peninsula geography only. Neither it nor the prose traces the particular final selected channel and terminal through-link. Actual terminal correspondence therefore remains material pending.
